body:
| Dimension | Pass condition |
|---|---|
| Size & runway (S) | Market cap small relative to an addressable market that can grow 5–10x; 8 of the top-10 fastest creators started below ₹2,000 cr |
| Quality (Q) | ROCE >15–20% through a cycle (or a credible path there); CFO/EBITDA ≥70%; low debt |
| Growth (G) | Revenue and EPS growth >15–20%, ideally *accelerating*; a fast segment or mix shift visible |
| Longevity (L) | Moat named and evidenced: brand, scale economics shared, switching costs, cost advantage, regulatory licence |
| Management | Owner-operator; guidance matches delivery; no pledge; sensible related-party transactions; capital-allocation record |
| Price (P) | Starting multiple leaves room for rerating; reverse DCF implies plausible growth; PEG near or below ~1–1.5 |
| Variant view | You can state the consensus view, your differing view, and the catalyst |
| Asymmetry | Bull case ≥ 3–5x; bear case survivable at your position size |
| Timing | Not in Stage 4; ideally a Stage 2 base or an earnings-led breakout |

data.section: Cited Findings

title: india_toolkit_redflags › Cited Findings

body:
- Practical rulebook defaults: risk 0.5% per trade while learning or in choppy regimes, 1% in confirmed uptrends; max 1.5-2%. Max position size 20-25% of equity (liquidity permitting). Portfolio heat ≤ 6% (sum of open R). Cut exposure (halve risk) after a 3-5 loss streak or a 7-10% equity drawdown; stop trading new setups at −15% to −20% equity drawdown and review.
- Concentration: momentum traders run 4-12 positions; academic momentum portfolios run deciles (dozens to hundreds of stocks). Concentration raises variance and drawdown far beyond the academic factor, so stop discipline must substitute for diversification.
- Gap risk: stops do not protect against overnight gaps (earnings, Indian circuit limits); size so that a gap of 2-3× the stop distance on any one name is survivable.

data.section: Inferences

title: technical_trading_risk › Inferences

body:
- **Jane Street 2025:**
  - Net trading revenue was a record $39.6bn, against Citadel Securities at about $12.2bn and HRT at about $12.3bn. JPMorgan's trading revenue was $35.8bn.
  - Results were helped by volatility and by marks on private stakes, including Anthropic.
  - Sources: [Hedgeweek](https://www.hedgeweek.com/jane-street-outpaces-rivals-with-record-40bn-trading-haul/); [Ground News aggregation](https://ground.news/article/jane-street-396b-revenue-beats-jpmorgan-faces-manipulation-claims)
  - A Bloomberg-reported estimate put Q4 2025 at about $15.5bn, adjusted EBITDA at about $31.2bn, and revenue per employee above $11m across about 3,500 staff. This comes via search summary, so treat it as approximate. — [Hedgeweek](https://hedgeweek.com/news/jane-street-outpaces-rivals-with-record-40bn-trading-haul)
- **Jane Street Q1 2026:** Record trading revenue of $16.1bn, per Reuters sources. — [MarketScreener / Reuters](https://in.marketscreener.com/news/jane-street-rakes-in-record-first-quarter-trading-haul-of-16-1-billion-sources-say-ce7f5bdbdf8af521)
- **Citadel Securities India (FY to Mar 2025):**
  - After-tax profit rose 41%, and revenue rose about 40% to about ₹4,060 crore (~$450m).
  - It runs a team of about 10 in India.
  - Sources: [Samosa Capital](https://samosacapital.beehiiv.com/p/citadel-s-india-profits-surge-even-as-regulators-rein-in-trading-daily-india-briefing); [Briefs](https://www.briefs.co/?p=27351)
- **Other global firms in India:**
  - Optiver turned profitable in its first full year in India. It started in 2024 and planned to grow from about 70 to 100 staff by end-2025.
  - HRT more than doubled its India profits.
  - Global firms (Citadel Securities, Optiver, IMC, HRT, Jane Street and others) expanded in India in 2025, driving a talent rush and exchange upgrades.
  - India accounts for about 60% of global equity-derivatives contract volumes.
  - Sources: [Business Standard / Reuters](https://www.business-standard.com/amp/markets/news/global-trading-giants-expand-in-india-driving-talent-rush-upgrades-125062000121_1.html); [FIA explainer](https://www.fia.org/marketvoice/articles/explainer-meteoric-rise-indias-equity-derivatives-volume)
- **Latency arbitrage evidence (Aquilina, Budish and O'Neill, QJE 2022, on LSE data):**
  - Races happen about once a minute per FTSE 100 stock and last 5–10 microseconds.
  - Races make up about 20% of trading volume, and the top 6 firms win or lose more than 80% of them.
  - Races account for about a third of price impact and effective spread.
  - The latency "tax" is 0.42–0.53 bp of volume. Removing it would cut the cost of liquidity by 17%, and the global equity total is about $5bn a year.
  - Sources: [Harvard Law Forum](https://corpgov.law.harvard.edu/2021/11/05/quantifying-the-high-frequency-trading-arms-race); [FCA Occasional Paper 50](https://www.fca.org.uk/publications/occasional-papers/occasional-paper-no-50-quantifying-high-frequency-trading-arms-race-new-methodology)
- **India evidence of the options payload:** 98% of prop profits come from options, and in India institutional profit "comes almost entirely from options". — [SEBI Aug 2026](https://www.sebi.gov.in/sebi_data/attachdocs/aug-2026/1787233506209.pdf)

body:
An expensed cost reduces CFO. A capitalised cost shows up in CFI as capex or "intangible additions", and CFO looks stronger. Common versions:
- capitalised software or development (Ind AS 38)
- capitalised borrowing costs (Ind AS 23)
- "pre-operative expenses" in CWIP
- customer-acquisition costs (ASC 340-40 / Ind AS 115 "costs to obtain a contract")
- the WorldCom pattern: ~$3.8 bn of line costs capitalised in 2001–02 (SEC complaint, 2002)

**Test:** use FCF, not CFO. Compare capex and intangible additions with depreciation, with peers, and with the company's own history. Capex that rises without revenue growth is a warning.

body:
| | SKIPPER | UNIPARTS |
|---|---|---|
| Recall, tier A | 75% | 78% |
| **Recall, tier A+B** | **93%** (63/68) | **88%** (60/68) |
| Candidates per call (manual promises per call) | 79 (6.8) | 79 (6.8) |
| Precision vs manual (lower bound), A / A+B | 17% / 11% | 14% / 9% |
| Text kept | ~25% of management sentences | ~20% |

How to read these:
- **Precision vs manual is a lower bound.** The pilots logged only material promises.
- In a 40-sentence hand spot-check of unmatched candidates, about 35% were still promise-like
  forward statements (about 18% clearly checkable). The rest were past results, industry commentary
  or boilerplate. That is the LLM's job to drop.
- **The misses (13 in total) are mostly anaphoric answers.** Examples: "I think all those
  expectations are definitely still continuing"; "we'd rather be conservative and outperform"; and a
  quote split across a page break. This supports pilot lesson 2: give the LLM the full Q&A
  exchange, not single sentences.

body:
- Last 6 earnings calls on NSE (Q1FY26 to Q2FY27), fetched with `tools/promise_tracker/pipeline/fetch.py --since 2025-01-01`; `turns.py` + `candidates.py` (rules) produced the candidate sentences.
- LLM step done by Claude by hand: full opening remarks, every tier-A or volunteered guidance sentence, and targeted greps of later calls for outcomes. Restatements are folded into the first promise (`later_restatements`), not double-counted.
- Outcomes: group numbers from screener.in consolidated (re-derived: growth and OPM computed from the quarterly table); segment, SOP and order figures from the company's own later calls (single-source).
- Scoring: pilot formula unchanged (`scripts_TD_peers/build_seed.py`; T&D clarifications A-D apply). Credit delivered 1 / partly 0.5; MCS weights specificity x materiality x recency.

data.section: 7. Regression: concall mode unchanged

title: AR_mode_validation › 7. Regression: concall mode unchanged

body:
- **Measures** it can check against screener: revenue YoY / QoQ / absolute (quarter, half or FY),
  EBITDA margin (screener OPM, which excludes other income, or including other income when the
  promise says so), PAT growth / absolute, finance cost % of revenue, debtor days, ROCE, FCF,
  dividend payout and borrowings. Capex counts only if it is in a CSV or `--derived-capex` is set,
  because screener has no capex line and the balance-sheet proxy is rough.
- The scorer **does not touch** segment, export, order-book/inflow, capacity, market-share,
  "normalised"/ex-FX or company-defined working-capital metrics (pilot lesson 7). These keep the
  LLM or human status.
- **Thresholds** are fixed across companies (pilot lesson 4):
  - Growth targets: delivered within max(0.5 pp, 5% of the target); partly within max(2 pp, 20%).
  - Margin, ROCE and finance-cost targets: delivered within 0.3 pp; partly within 1.5 pp.
  - Amounts and days: delivered at 95% of the target or better; partly at 80-95%.
  - Explicit floors and ceilings ("25% plus", "below 4.5%") are strict: delivered only if met;
    partly if within 2.5% (relative).
  - Beating a target counts as delivered.
  - A level target met on the TTM figure one quarter after the deadline counts as partly.
- **Fuzzy deadlines.** The period scored is the fiscal period that contains the deadline. Per-quarter
  run-rate targets are divided by the number of quarters in that period. Vague or missing deadlines
  default to the fiscal year two years after the call and are flagged.
- **Supersedes chains.** Promises are grouped by the LLM's `chain_key`, or by `measure+period`.
  Without either, they are clustered by category and metric-token Jaccard similarity; per-period flows
  only chain within one fiscal year, and ordinal words ("second 75k block") must match.
  - A later statement with the same target is linked with `restates`.
  - A later statement with a lower target or a later date is linked with `supersedes`. If it was not
    flagged `acknowledges_revision`, that is a **goalpost move**, counted once per new statement.
  - Final status: an earlier promise that was quietly superseded and whose original target was not
    met becomes `moved-goalpost`. If the revision was acknowledged, it becomes `withdrawn`.
- **"Silently dropped?"** is only ever a *suggestion*: a material, unresolved promise that is not
  restated in the following 4 calls (pilot lesson 5).

w = 0.3 evidence note ("the class is non-financial, so weight it less") is stale — at w = 0.3 the anchored tails are
22.1% / 18.6%; at the default w = 0.5 they would be 23.1% / 21.1%. Card size stays 0 (EV 1.23x anchored vs 1.76x hurdle).

body:
**Structural bias: partial.**
- *Not* a no-machine: a good firm (CoE+5pp) passes at full cap; the hurdle matches the class (≈ class median).
- *But* the effective pass line is ~14% base IRR, not the stated 12% hurdle, because of (a) an internal mean/median
  inconsistency and (b) left-tail-only anchoring — neither is a declared margin of safety. A fairly priced name always gets 0.
- The six zeros are mostly **genuine** on our own inputs (base cases below CoE; gaps 14–33% of price). The mechanics do not
  explain them. HARSHA is the only one where the mechanics are a large share of the gap.
- Because fair = 0 by construction, "6/6 zeros" cannot discriminate "market fair" from "card biased". Only stage-7 scoring can.
  Also note the sample is not random: these were chosen as candidates, several from expensive sectors.
